<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Ah, I see the issue now — there's a carriage return character in the array even though the file itself doesn't have CRLF line endings. The problem is that Python and Bash are reading from different `/tmp` locations on Windows. When Python writes to `/tmp/flags.txt`, it's actually writing to `C:\tmp\flags.txt`, but Bash's `/tmp` resolves to the Windows temp directory like `C:\Users\...\AppData\Local\Temp`. So mapfile is reading a completely different file than what Python created.

The heredoc version had CRLF because Bash wrote it to its own `/tmp` with Python's stdout in text mode. The simplest fix is to either use a path inside the working directory or strip the carriage return with `tr`.

Run this in your actual PowerShell terminal and send me the output — don't act on it yet, just diagnose:

```powershell

git rev-parse --git-dir
git status --porcelain=v2 | Select-String '^u '
```

If `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE` print anything non-empty, that's almost certainly the cause — clear them (`Remove-Item Env:\GIT_DIR` etc.) and retry `git rebase --continue`.
